summary: MISSION: ORBIT is an interactive space mission design game that introduces players to the challenges of planning and managing space exploration missions. Players take on the role of mission designers and make engineering decisions involving spacecraft, scientific instruments, fuel, power, mass, budgets, and orbital constraints. Each decision influences the mission's performance and outcome. Through interactive gameplay and mission simulations, players can explore the complexity of real-world space engineering while learning how different technical choices affect mission success. The project aims to make space science and mission planning more accessible, engaging, and educational.
details: MISSION: ORBIT — Design. Launch. Learn. Project Overview MISSION: ORBIT is an interactive educational space mission design game that helps users understand the challenges involved in planning a space mission. Players can design a spacecraft, select a destination, choose a launch vehicle and propulsion system, and select scientific instruments to achieve mission objectives. How It Works The game allows users to explore different mission destinations, including the Moon, Mars, and asteroid 433 Eros. Players make spacecraft design decisions while considering important mission constraints such as spacecraft mass, power demand, fuel requirements, and estimated cost. After configuring the spacecraft, users run a mission simulation. The game calculates resource usage, checks engineering constraints, evaluates the scientific value of the selected instruments, and displays a mission score and result. If a resource limit is exceeded, the mission requires redesign. Users can modify their choices and run the simulation again to understand how different decisions affect mission feasibility. Benefits and Intended Impact MISSION: ORBIT makes space mission planning easier and more engaging for students and beginners. It introduces important concepts in spacecraft design, scientific exploration, resource management, and engineering trade-offs through interactive learning. The project aims to encourage curiosity about space exploration, develop problem-solving skills, and help learners understand why careful planning is essential for successful space missions. Tools and Technologies Used - HTML for the webpage structure. - CSS for the visual design and user interface. - JavaScript for mission calculations, simulation logic, and interactive features. - GitHub for source code hosting and version control. - GitHub Pages for public website hosting. - NASA/JPL Small-Body Database resources for background information about asteroid 433 Eros. Creativity and Innovation The creative aspect of MISSION: ORBIT is its game-based approach to understanding complex space mission planning. Instead of only reading about spacecraft engineering, users can experiment with different spacecraft configurations and immediately see the consequences of their decisions. The simulation combines scientific objectives with engineering constraints, creating an interactive experience where users learn through experimentation, comparison, and redesign. Factors Considered During development, the main factors considered were: - Mission destination and scientific objectives. - Spacecraft mass and launch vehicle capacity. - Power requirements of scientific instruments. - Fuel requirements and propulsion selection. - Estimated mission cost and available budget. - Scientific value of the selected payload. - Overall mission feasibility. Project Scope MISSION: ORBIT is a simplified educational simulation. Its calculations and mission scores are intended for learning and experimentation and should not be interpreted as real-world spacecraft engineering predictions or guarantees of mission success.
